claim: Simonis' age at the 1299 marriage (five? six? seven?)
ref: Gregoras, Historia Byzantina VI.9, Bonn vol. 1 p. 203 (Greek lines 16-18; Latin 'quintum iam annum agente')
quote_orig: μηνύει τῷ Κράλῃ περὶ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ θυγατρὸς Σιμωνίδος, πέμπτον τῆς ἡλικίας ἀγούσης ἔτος, ἵν᾽ ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνῳ λαβόντι τρέφοιτο, μέχρις ἂν ἐς τὸν νομιζόμενον ἔλθῃ τοῦ γάμου χρόνον κἄπειτα εἴη σύζυγος αὐτῷ τοῦ λοιποῦ.
quote_en: (Latin, Boivin) 'coactus Imperator illi de Simonide filia sua significat, quintum iam annum agente, ut ab illo domi accepta aleretur, donec ad nubilem aetatem perveniret, ac deinde coniux esset.'
own_translation_en: The emperor informs the Serb about his daughter Simonis, who was in the fifth year of her age, so that, taken by him, she might be raised until she came to the customary time of marriage, and then be his wife from then on.
edition: Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 1, 1829 (Schopen/Bekker); Greek with Latin version by Boivin (1702), public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Gregoras states the girl was in her fifth year of age when the emperor notified the Serb, and that she was to be raised in the Serb's household until the customary marriage time.
limits: Gregoras gives no exact birth date; 'fifth year' is his age reckoning. The Greek word for marriage age is only 'the customary time', not a number. Greek read from page image (p. 203, Greek column).

claim: Simonis' age and Milutin's age in 1299; 'the Serb was fifty' (draft's Milutin ~50)
status: PARTLY VERIFIED (Gregoras: she was an infant; he was forty and about five years older than her father)
ref: Gregoras VI.10, Bonn vol. 1 p. 204 (Greek lines 9-12; Latin 'infantulam', 'quadragenarius', 'socero quinque circiter annos natu maior')
quote_orig: ἐπάνεισε τὴν Σιμωνίδα λαβὼν βρέφος οὖσαν τεσσαρακοντούτης τυγχάνων αὐτὸς καὶ τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ πενθεροῦ καθ᾽ ἡλικίαν προήκων πέντε ἔτεσιν ἔγγιστα.
quote_en: (Latin, Boivin) 'secumque Simonidem infantulam abducit, ipse quadragenarius, et socero quinque circiter annos natu maior.'
own_translation_en: He took Simonis back with him while she was still an infant, he himself being forty years old and about five years older than the emperor, his father-in-law.
edition: Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 1, 1829 (Schopen/Bekker); Greek with Latin version by Boivin (1702), public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Gregoras calls Simonis an infant when she left for Serbia and gives Milutin's age as about forty, roughly five years older than Andronikos II.
limits: The Greek is 'forty' (not fifty). 'Fifty' appears only in the editorial Latin summary (see S1-09) and in Possinus's note (Gregoras vol. 2, Bonn note on p. 204), which argues Milutin was nearer 45. Greek read from image.

claim: Simonis was five (or six) at the marriage; Pachymeres' independent age
ref: Pachymeres, De Andronico Palaeologo, Bonn vol. 2 pp. 274-275 (running head 'L. III' as printed, p. 275; chapter (31))
quote_orig: ἦν οὖν πάνυ ἀστεῖον τοῦτο τὸ ϑυγάτριον, οὔπω τὸν ἕκτον παραλλάττον ἐνιαυτόν, ἀγαπητὸν μὲν ἑαυτῷ, ἀγαπητὸν δ᾽ ἐκτόπως καὶ τῇ μητρί.
quote_en: (Latin, Poussines) 'filiola, quam habebat oppido festivam, nondum sexenni maiorem, sibi pariter et matri longe carissimam.'
own_translation_en: This little daughter was very charming, not yet passing her sixth year, dear to himself and exceedingly dear to her mother too.
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 2, 1835; Latin version by Poussines (Possinus), 1666, public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Pachymeres says the girl was not yet six, i.e. five or about to turn six, when she was betrothed to Milutin in 1298-99.
limits: Pachymeres' age is a description of the betrothal stage, not of the 1299 wedding itself. Possinus's note in Gregoras cites this passage as 'lib. II cap. XXXI'; the Bonn running head printed on p. 275 reads 'L. III'. Greek and Latin read from page image (PDF page 288 = Bonn p. 275).

claim: Gregoras: CONSUMMATION at age EIGHT; made her unable to bear children
status: VERIFIED (Gregoras: eight years old; womb injured; no further offspring possible). Timing NOT stated.
ref: Gregoras, Historia Byzantina VII.5, Bonn vol. 1 p. 243 (Greek lines 8-9; Latin 'cum puella octo annos nata congressus matricem eius laesit')
quote_orig: τῇ μὲν γὰρ θυγατρὶ ὀκταετεῖ πλέον ἢ τεσσαρακοντούτης τοῦ Κράλη μιγεὶς βλαβῆναι τὴν ταύτης πέπραχε μήτραν, ὡς μηδὲ γονὴν ἐξ ἐκείνης ἔτι δύνασθαι γίγνεσθαι.
quote_en: (Latin, Boivin) 'Crales enim quadragenario maior cum puella octo annos nata congressus matricem eius laesit, ut foetum nullum posthac edere posset.'
own_translation_en: For, having had intercourse with his eight-year-old daughter (sic: the Serb, more than forty years old), the Kralis injured her womb, so that she could no longer bear offspring from him.
edition: Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 1, 1829 (Schopen/Bekker); Greek with Latin version by Boivin (1702), public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Gregoras states that Milutin, over forty, had intercourse with Simonis when she was eight, which injured her womb so that she could no longer conceive.
limits: Gregoras does not date this act to 1299 or to any time after the wedding; the sentence sits in his account of Irene's later schemes to secure heirs (c. 1300s). The Latin and Greek are restrained ('congressus', 'μιγείς'); I give no further wording. Greek read from page image; the word for the Serb's age is partly blurred in the scan (print reads 'τεσσαρακοντούτης'). The Bonn margin 'A.C. 1282-1328' is the reign range, not the date of the event.

claim: Patriarch's objections (immaturity of the bride, oaths, legitimacy of prior marriages)
status: VERIFIED (Pachymeres: Emperor's account of obstacles, incl. the girl's immaturity)
ref: Pachymeres, De Andronico Palaeologo, Bonn vol. 2 p. 279 (Greek lines 15-17); Latin 'sexennem aetate connubio intempestivam' (p. 279)
quote_orig: τό τ᾽ ἐφ᾽ ὁρκωμοσίαις τὸν κράλην φρικταῖς τὴν τοῦ Τερτερῆ προσλαβέσθαι, τό τε νομίμως δοκεῖν συνεζεῦχϑαι, ἥ τ᾽ ἀφηλικίωσις τῆς νεάνιδος, καὶ τὸ φϑάσαι τὸν Σέρβον τὴν τἀδελφοῦ Στεφάνου γυναικαδέλφην
quote_en: (Latin, Poussines, p. 279 area) 'virgunculae ... plane videri sexennem aetate connubio intempestivam' (the patriarch's view that a six-year-old girl was plainly unfit for marriage)
own_translation_en: ...that he [the Serb] should take Terteres' sister by terrible oaths, that the marriage seemed lawfully contracted, the immaturity of the young girl, and that the Serb had got in first with his brother Stephen's sister-in-law...
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 2, 1835; Latin version by Poussines (Possinus), 1666, public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Pachymeres lists among the emperor's obstacles the oaths concerning Terteres' sister, the apparent legal validity of Milutin's earlier marriages, and the girl's immaturity (ἀφηλικίωσις). He presents these as the reasons the patriarch's side would press.
limits: Pachymeres narrates these as the emperor's own calculation, so 'the Patriarch objected on these grounds' is a paraphrase, not his explicit words here. The Latin 'sexennem' phrase is Poussines's rendering on p. 279 and I did not confirm the Greek of it on the image.

claim: Patriarch opposed; Church reasoning; Milutin's status ('first wife' not the Church's rule)
status: VERIFIED (Patriarch opposed; wedding performed by Archbishop of Achrida; Patriarch absent)
ref: Pachymeres, Bonn vol. 2 p. 280 (Greek lines 4-10, 'ἀμιξία'); p. 285 (Greek lines 19-21)
quote_orig: ἐκκλησίᾳ μὴ ἀνάγκην ἐχούσῃ καθ᾽ ἱερὰς τελετὰς διὰ τὴν ἀμιξίαν ἐκείνου μιμνήσκεσθαι
quote_en: (Latin, p. 280) '... dynastae videlicet ritus a Graeco peregrini; quem ideo licet contingeret fieri generum imperatoris, in sacris officiis memoraturi nominatim ecclesiastici non forent...'
own_translation_en: (p. 280) ...since the Church has no need to remember him in the sacred rites on account of his [lack of communion/ 'ἀμιξία']...; (p. 285) 'And also from the Archbishop of Achrida [Pacharios/Macharios as printed], after the usual sacred rites were completed, he received the honours due...'
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 2, 1835; Latin version by Poussines (Possinus), 1666, public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Pachymeres says the emperor avoided discussing the marriage with Patriarch John and sent him to Selymbria; the emperor's reasoning was that the Church need not name the Serb in the liturgy because of his estrangement. The wedding blessing in Thessalonica came from the Archbishop of Achrida (Ohrid), not the Patriarch. Possinus's 1300 summary (Bonn p. 850) says the patriarch then lived in Pammakaristos 'as if a private person' after grieving over the affinity; that summary is editorial and not yet checked against Pachymeres' Greek.
limits: 'ἀμιξία' is my rendering as 'lack of communion/estrangement'; the Achrida prelate's name in the Greek is printed as Παχαρίου or Μαχαρίου and I could not confirm the initial on the image. Pachymeres does not say the Church formally approved the marriage in these pages; the 'first wife' legal argument is presented as the emperor's, not as an ecclesiastical ruling (see S1-07).

claim: The 'first wife' loophole (wives 2 and 3 'not real wives'; first wife's death freed him)
status: VERIFIED (Pachymeres gives the argument; Eudokia refused it)
ref: Pachymeres, Bonn vol. 2 p. 273 (Greek lines 9-14); p. 274 (Greek line 14-15: refusal)
quote_orig: ἐπεὶ καὶ προτέρα τεθνηκυῖα ἠκούετο καὶ τὸ ἀπὸ τοῦδε τῇ συνοικησούσῃ νομίμῳ εἶναι μετὰ τὴν πρώτην ἐδίδοτο, τῶν ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ὡς νόϑων ἀπηλλοτριωμένων
quote_en: (Latin, Poussines) 'qua vera comperta, manifestum erat solutum esse illum ac liberum ad novum rite connubium ineundum.'
own_translation_en: ...since it was reported that the first wife had died, and it was granted that the woman who would now cohabit with him would be lawful after the first, the marriages in between being regarded as bastard...
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 2, 1835; Latin version by Poussines (Possinus), 1666, public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Pachymeres describes the emperor's legal argument to Eudokia: the first wife's death made Milutin free for a lawful marriage, and the wives in between were 'as bastards'. Eudokia refused to be the Serb's wife.
limits: This is an argument put by the emperor to Eudokia, reported by Pachymeres; it is not a canon of the Church. Greek read from image (p. 273) and Latin from the same page.

claim: Gregoras says the wait was until she was TWELVE (draft's 'condition to wait until twelve')
status: UNVERIFIED / NOT FOUND in Gregoras or Pachymeres as read. Gregoras VI.9 says 'until the customary marriage time', no number.
ref: Gregoras VI.9 p. 203 (Greek 18-19); Pachymeres p. 276 Latin 'usque ad nubilem aetatem'
quote_orig: μέχρις ἂν ἐς τὸν νομιζόμενον ἔλθῃ τοῦ γάμου χρόνον
quote_en: 'until she should come to the customary/legal time of marriage' (own literal translation)
own_translation_en: until she came to the customary time of marriage
edition: Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 1, 1829 (Schopen/Bekker); Greek with Latin version by Boivin (1702), public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: No numerical age (twelve or otherwise) is given in Gregoras VI.9 or in Pachymeres for the waiting period. Pachymeres' Latin says she was to be raised in the Serb's house 'until marriageable age'.
limits: Negative result over the texts I read; I did not read Gregoras' Latin-Greek notes for any other 'twelve'. Gregoras IX.13 (S1-10) gives a 12-year-old in a different marriage (below). The editorial Latin summary (S1-09) says 'usque ad puberem aetatem' (until puberty), not 12.

claim: Editorial summary: 'eight' and 'nearly fifty' (what the draft may be drawing on)
status: CONTRADICTED as a description of the narrative (editorial gloss, not Pachymeres' text)
ref: Possinus, Observationes Pachymerianae, Chronologicus Lib. III, 1299 row, Bonn vol. 2 p. 849 (PDF page 866 of georgiipachymer00pousgoog.pdf)
quote_orig: Imperator Thessalonicae, tractatu affinitatis cum crale Serbiae concluso ... puellulam vix octennem viro prope quinquagenario ... custodiendam videlicet intactam usque ad puberem aetatem (quem tamen Gregoras l. 7 scribit festinanda per intemperantem expectandi impatientiam defloratione virgunculae inhabilem illam gignendis postea liberis reddidisse.)
quote_en: (Latin, Possinus) 'Emperor at Thessalonica ... gives his daughter Simonis as bride to the Serb ... a little girl scarcely eight, to a man nearly fifty ... to be kept intact until puberty (though Gregoras, book 7, writes that by hasty defloration ... he made her unfit to bear children later).'
edition: Georgii Pachymeris De Michaele et Andronico Palaeologis libri tredecim, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 2, 1835; Latin version by Poussines (Possinus), 1666, public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF; the chronological table is Possinus's, not Pachymeres'
what_it_says: The 17th-century editor's chronological table gives the 1299 wedding as 'scarcely eight' and the groom as 'nearly fifty', citing Gregoras VII (= VII.5) for the later defloration.
limits: Editor's summary, not Pachymeres' or Gregoras' narrative. It conflicts with both primary narratives (five/six for Simonis; forty for Milutin). The summary's 'eight' is what Gregoras' VII.5 says of the intercourse, not of the marriage. Read from page image.

claim: (side finding) another marriage with a twelve-year-old bride
status: PARTLY VERIFIED as a separate passage; NOT about Simonis
ref: Gregoras, Historia Byzantina IX.13, Bonn vol. 1 pp. 467-468 (Greek 'τῆς Καίσαρος θυγατρὶ'; Latin 'Caesaris filiam annos natam duodecim ipse quinquagenarius duxisset')
quote_orig: ἐπεὶ δ᾽ αὐτὸς μὲν τῇ τοῦ Καίσαρος θυγατρὶ συνεζύγη, πεντηκοντούτης ἀνὴρ κόρῃ δωδέκατον ἀγούσῃ τὸν χρόνον, καὶ πρὶν τῷ παιδὶ γυναῖκα ἀγαγέσθαι, παιδοποιεῖν ἤρξατο
quote_en: (Latin, Boivin) 'Sed cum Caesaris filiam annos natam duodecim ipse quinquagenarius duxisset, et priusquam filio despondisset uxorem, liberos ex illa suscepisset...'
own_translation_en: When he himself had married the daughter of the Kaisar, being a fifty-year-old man, the girl being in her twelfth year, and before he took a wife for his son, he began to have children with the Kaisar's daughter...
edition: Nicephori Gregorae Byzantina historia, ed. I. Bekker, Bonn (Corpus SHB) vol. 1, 1829 (Schopen/Bekker); Greek with Latin version by Boivin (1702), public domain; scan Google/archive.org, page image read from PDF
what_it_says: Gregoras describes a later marriage (Milutin aged fifty to a twelve-year-old, 'daughter of the Kaisar'), which is a different bride from Simonis (who is 'the emperor's daughter' in the same book). Relevant to the draft only as a further age data point in Gregoras; should not be conflated with Simonis.
limits: Greek from OCR, not yet checked against the page image. The identity of 'the Kaisar's daughter' is not given in the sentence; I did not identify her.
